title: Offer a list JSON envelope that can carry non-item data
lead: Give `slicer list --json` an opt-in object form so agents that read only the list can see sibling-only open items, without changing the array every current consumer parses.
findings_note: s223 landing 2026-10-05: list --json is a bare array, so sibling-only items could only go in status --json
boundary: **Not in this slice:** changing the default `list --json` shape, `status`, `next` or `check`, adding other kinds of sibling data, or changing which sibling rows count as `only_in_sibling` (s223 settled that).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `list --json` is a bare array of items (`docs/agents.md`, the `list` row). s223 added sibling-only open items to `list` text and to `status --json` as `only_in_sibling`, and left `list --json` unchanged: a top-level key cannot be added to an array without breaking its consumers, including the slicer skill's own `list --json --lean` calls. An agent that reads only `list --json` therefore cannot see a sibling-only item, and has to call `status`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `test_ListJson_NoEnvelopeFlag_StaysABareArray`: with a sibling-only item present, `list --json` is exactly today's array.
2. `test_ListJson_Envelope_ItemsAndOnlyInSibling`: `list --json --envelope` is `{"items": [...], "only_in_sibling": [...]}`. `items` equals the bare array for the same filters. `only_in_sibling` equals `status --json`'s list.
3. `test_ListJson_Envelope_RespectsFiltersSortsAndLean`: `--all`, `--status`, `--tree`, `--pass`, `--sort` and `--lean` apply to `items` as they do to the array. `only_in_sibling` is `[]` when empty, so the shape is stable.
4. `test_ListEnvelope_WithoutJson_IsUsage`: `--envelope` without `--json` exits 2 with code `usage`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Settle the shape with the owner before building; do not infer. The leading candidate is an opt-in `--envelope` flag on `list`, used with `--json`, because it changes nothing for existing callers. Alternatives to weigh: wrap by default and treat it as a breaking change with a changelog note, or leave `status` as the only home for this data.

Reuse the one pass over siblings that `store.sibling_work` already makes, so `list` still enumerates worktrees once and reads each sibling index once (`test_List_EnumeratesOnceAndReadsEachSiblingIndexOnce`). Document the flag and the shape in both docs and the changelog.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` run from a worktree, `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, with the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
